title: A morphism of inverse systems induces a (non-unique) morphism of derived limits
statement: Let $\mathcal D$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category], and let $(K_n,f_n)_{n\geq1}$, $(K'_n,f'_n)_{n\geq1}$ be inverse systems of objects of $\mathcal D$ [def-weil-inverse-system] whose products exist [def-weil-category-product], with transition endomorphisms $1-s$, $1-s'$ [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism]. Let $K\xrightarrow{p}\prod_nK_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nK_n\xrightarrow{\delta}K[1]$ and $K'\xrightarrow{p'}\prod_nK'_n\xrightarrow{1-s'}\prod_nK'_n\xrightarrow{\delta'}K'[1]$ be distinguished triangles (Roos triangles; $K$, $K'$ are derived limits [def-weil-derived-limit]), and let $(\varphi_n):(K_n,f_n)\to(K'_n,f'_n)$ be a morphism of inverse systems. Then there exists a morphism $\varphi:K\to K'$ with $p'\circ\varphi=(\prod_n\varphi_n)\circ p$ and $\varphi[1]\circ\delta=\delta'\circ\prod_n\varphi_n$, i.e. $(\varphi,\prod_n\varphi_n,\prod_n\varphi_n)$ is a morphism of triangles. The morphism $\varphi$ is in general not unique.

source.place: Stacks Project, Derived Categories, Remark Tag 0H9J (remark-functoriality-derived-limit), derived.tex line 10525, in the case $m(n)=n$ where $a'=a''=\prod_na_n$: "by TR3 we obtain the dotted arrow producing a morphism of distinguished triangles. We warn the reader that the map $K\to L$ is not unique."

proof.text: Put $P=\prod_nK_n$, $P\prime=\prod_nK\prime_n$ and $a=\prod_n\varphi_n:P\to P\prime$. By the definition of the product morphism, $\mathrm{pr}\prime_n\circ a=\varphi_n\circ\mathrm{pr}_n$. Consequently $\mathrm{pr}\prime_n\circ s\prime\circ a=f\prime_n\circ\varphi_{n+1}\circ\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}=\varphi_n\circ f_n\circ\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}=\mathrm{pr}\prime_n\circ a\circ s$, using exactly the compatibility equation for a morphism of inverse systems. Uniqueness in the product universal property gives $s\prime\circ a=a\circ s$. Subtracting from $a$ in the additive category gives $(1-s\prime)\circ a=a\circ(1-s)$. This also follows directly from the compatibility clause of def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0H9J, remark-functoriality-derived-limit, with m(n)=n; Tag 0145, definition-triangulated-category, TR2 and TR3

proof.text: Rotate each given distinguished triangle once using TR2 in def-weil-triangulated-category, obtaining $P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\xrightarrow{\delta}K[1]\xrightarrow{-p[1]}P[1]$ and $P\prime\xrightarrow{1-s\prime}P\prime\xrightarrow{\delta\prime}K\prime[1]\xrightarrow{-p\prime[1]}P\prime[1]$. The square on their first arrows, with vertical arrows $a,a$, commutes by step 1. Apply TR3, as stated in that same definition, to get $c:K[1]\to K\prime[1]$ with $c\circ\delta=\delta\prime\circ a$ and $a[1]\circ(-p[1])=(-p\prime[1])\circ c$. These are direct applications of the two defining axioms, rather than a separate triangle-completion lemma.

source.place: Tag 0H9J, remark-functoriality-derived-limit, with m(n)=n; Tag 0145, definition-triangulated-category, TR2 and TR3

proof.text: Since $[1]$ is an additive autoequivalence in def-weil-triangulated-category, it is full and faithful: choose $\varphi:K\to K\prime$ with $\varphi[1]=c$. Cancel the minus signs in the last equation of step 2 to get $a[1]\circ p[1]=p\prime[1]\circ\varphi[1]$. Faithfulness, together with preservation of composition by $[1]$, yields $a\circ p=p\prime\circ\varphi$. The other equation of step 2 is $\varphi[1]\circ\delta=\delta\prime\circ a$. Together with the middle square from step 1 these are precisely the three squares defining the required morphism of triangles. TR3 supplies an existence assertion, with no uniqueness condition; the final sentence of Tag 0H9J warns that the resulting map need not be unique, so this construction does not specify a canonical map or assert functorial choices.
